records.name: AiFi
records.description: AiFi: AI-powered spatial intelligence platform enabling checkout-free shopping for retail, airports, stadiums, and QSRs with computer vision.
records.about: Based in Burlingame, California, AiFi develops an artificial intelligence and computer vision platform that enables commercial retailers to operate checkout-free autonomous stores. The enterprise software utilizes a network of cameras to create real-time 3D digital twins of physical spaces, tracking shopper behavior and automatically processing payments without shelf sensors. The company operates with a workforce of over 160 employees and has deployed its technology in more than 300 retail locations across 16 countries. Backed by investors such as Qualcomm Ventures and Verizon Ventures, the enterprise has raised over $80 million in total funding and reached an estimated valuation of $250 million in late 2025. Its spatial intelligence solutions are utilized by major retail and entertainment operators globally, including ALDI, Carrefour, and Morrisons. AiFi was originally founded in 2016 by Steve Gu and Ying Zheng.

records.name: Air
records.description: Air: Cloud-based visual workspace and digital asset management (DAM) platform for creative and marketing teams, with AI features.
records.about: Air is a Brooklyn, New York-based software company that develops a cloud-based visual workspace and digital asset management platform for creative and marketing teams. Operating on a B2B SaaS subscription model, the platform provides centralized image and video organization, automated tagging, and version control to replace traditional cloud storage systems. The startup serves tens of thousands of users and has raised over $28 million in total venture funding, which includes an $18 million Series A round secured in late 2021. Air is backed by prominent investors such as Tiger Global, Lerer Hippeau, and the Slack Fund, while its enterprise customer base features consumer brands like Sweetgreen and The Infatuation. The company recently integrated artificial intelligence capabilities into its software to enable smart search functions and automated visual tagging. Air was founded in 2017 by Shane Hegde and Tyler Strand.

records.name: AI Hay
records.location: Ho Chi Minh City, NA - Vietnam, Vietnam
records.description: AI Hay: AI-powered knowledge discovery platform combining generative AI with social networking for Vietnamese users, focused on local content and culture.
records.about: AI Hay is a Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam-based technology startup that develops an AI-powered knowledge discovery platform and conversational search engine tailored for the Vietnamese language. The consumer application combines generative artificial intelligence with interactive social networking features, processing more than 100 million user questions monthly. The company has accumulated over 15 million application downloads, ranking among the top five global AI applications by total download volume in early 2025. AI Hay has raised over $18 million in total venture capital funding, including a $10 million Series A round backed by Argor Capital, Square Peg, and Northstar Ventures. The enterprise also maintains strategic technology partnerships with AWS and NVIDIA to support the development of its proprietary language models. The organization was founded in 2021 by co-founders Chuong Nguyen, Duc Tran, and Hiep Nguyen.

records.name: AiVF
records.description: AiVF: AI software platform using machine learning and computer vision for IVF clinics to automate embryo grading and improve success rates.
records.about: Based in Tel Aviv, Israel, AiVF is a medical technology company that develops artificial intelligence and computer vision software to automate embryo grading and improve in vitro fertilization success rates. The company's flagship software-as-a-service platform, EMA, analyzes time-lapse videos of embryos to help clinicians select the most viable options, operating 50 times faster and 48 percent more accurately than manual human evaluation. The technology is currently deployed across more than 40 fertility clinics and laboratory networks throughout Europe, Asia, Australia, and the Americas. AiVF has raised over $25 million in total funding, backed by institutional investors including Insight Partners, Altaroc, and 166 2nd Financial Services. In early 2024, the enterprise expanded its hardware capabilities by acquiring Australian medical device manufacturer Genea Biomedx. The company was founded in 2018 by Daniella Gilboa and Prof. Daniel Seidman.

records.name: Aive
records.description: Aive: Generative AI video technology platform automating post-production, generating multiple formats for brands, agencies, and creative teams.
records.about: Based in Paris, France, Aive is a software-as-a-service company that provides an artificial intelligence platform to automate video post-production and distribution for enterprise brands, marketing teams, and creative agencies. The business-to-business platform utilizes proprietary multimodal generative technology to automatically adapt, format, and localize existing source videos into multiple lengths and aspect ratios optimized for various social media and digital advertising channels. Operating with a workforce of approximately 20 employees and generating under $5 million in annual revenue, the company recently expanded its commercial operations into the United States market. The startup has secured approximately €12 million in total funding from prominent venture capital firms and angel investors, including Sequoia Capital, Invus, Kima Ventures, and Eventbrite co-founder Renaud Visage. Aive was founded in 2019 by former Teads executive Olivier Reynaud and former Adyoulike executive Rudy Lellouche.

records.name: Aira
records.description: Aira: Clean energy technology company providing heat pumps and home energy solutions for residential homeowners in Europe, focused on decarbonizing heating.
records.about: Based in Stockholm, Sweden, Aira is a clean energy technology company that develops and distributes air source heat pumps, solar panels, and battery storage solutions through a direct-to-consumer subscription model. The vertically integrated business provides residential homeowners with hardware, intelligent controls, and professional installation services requiring zero upfront costs. Operating at a €200 million revenue run-rate, the enterprise manages a 220,000-square-meter manufacturing facility in Poland and maintains a workforce of 1,200 employees across 18 regional hubs. To finance its ongoing expansion into the United Kingdom, Germany, and Italy, the company secured €145 million in Series B equity funding from lead investors Altor, Kinnevik, Temasek, and Lingotto. The firm also acquired the British installation company All Seasons Energy to accelerate its regional deployment capabilities. Aira was founded in 2022 by the impact company builder Vargas Holding.

records.name: Aire
records.location: 1300 I St NW Ste 400E, Washington, District of Columbia 20005, US
records.description: Aire: Fintech company providing AI-driven alternative credit scoring for lenders, enabling inclusive credit decisions for consumers with thin histories.
records.about: Based in London, England, Aire is a financial technology company that develops alternative credit scoring software to help lenders assess consumers with limited credit histories. The business-to-business software platform utilizes artificial intelligence to conduct interactive virtual interviews and gather first-party contextual data directly from applicants. Prior to its acquisition, the enterprise scaled to a peak of approximately 50 employees and secured roughly $12 million in total venture capital funding, including an $11 million Series B round in 2019. The startup attracted investment from Crane Venture Partners and Experian, while serving corporate partners such as Toyota Financial Services and N Brown Group. In February 2021, the digital bank Zopa acquired the company to integrate its proprietary assessment technology into its own consumer lending ecosystem. Aire was founded in 2014 by Aneesh Varma, Taj Rihal, and Jon Bundy.

records.name: aito.ai
records.about: Aito.ai provides a predictive database that integrates machine learning directly into applications, enabling users to query predictions with standard SQL. The platform utilizes existing relational datasets to deliver immediate predictions and recommendations, streamlining intelligent feature creation. This solution facilitates robust decision automation within cloud environments. The company was founded on the insight that prevalent machine learning tools often create high barriers, hindering rapid development. Aito.ai aimed to democratize predictive analytics, simplifying how developers embed intelligence. This core principle facilitates quicker idea validation and efficient prototyping by abstracting complex ML processes. Aito.ai targets developers prioritizing rapid market entry, alongside non-technical and Robotic Process Automation operators. Its vision focuses on making predictive intelligence broadly accessible, empowering users to integrate sophisticated decision automation. The company aims to establish machine learning as an intuitive, integrated component of daily data operations.

records.name: AiV
records.description: AiV: Develops intelligent automation systems with AI, computer vision, optomechatronics for industrial visual inspection, quality control, manufacturing.
records.about: AiV is a Houston, Texas-based global master distributor of high-quality valves and actuators that provides full-service intelligent automation capabilities exclusively to supply houses and industrial distributors worldwide. The wholesale distribution company supports complex visual inspection and manufacturing operations across the oil and gas, power generation, chemical, petrochemical, refining, pulp and paper, and water treatment sectors. Operating from 10 global locations including recently expanded facilities in Canada and the United Kingdom, the enterprise maintains a 320,000-square-foot primary warehouse and holds over $100 million in worldwide inventory. The organization employs approximately 400 people to manage its specialized hardware-software systems, exotic alloy products, and technology integration services for industrial automation and quality assurance. Executive leadership includes Chief Executive Officer Trey Cook and Chief Financial Officer Ryan Loving, who also oversee operations for partner entity GCM. AiV was founded in 1991.

records.name: AIM
records.description: AIM: AI platform for heavy equipment, automates excavation, grading, material movement for construction, mining, and climate resilience.
records.about: AIM is a technology enterprise that develops an artificial intelligence-powered software platform to automate heavy equipment for excavation, grading, and material movement operations. The organization builds advanced perception, planning, and control systems designed specifically to modernize traditional earthmoving machinery used across the construction, mining, and climate resilience sectors. By integrating these autonomous capabilities into industrial vehicles, the business provides technological solutions intended to mitigate ongoing labor shortages and support large-scale infrastructure development. The proprietary system functions by processing environmental data to guide complex physical tasks, allowing standard construction fleets to operate with increased autonomy and precision in unpredictable outdoor environments. This core automation technology targets the operational inefficiencies of manual heavy machinery deployment by shifting reliance from human operators to algorithmic navigation. AIM was established in 2020 by founder and chief executive officer Adam Sadilek.

records.name: AI@X
records.description: AI@X: Provides AI assessment and certification services, performing general and attack assessments to protect AI systems for businesses.
records.about: AI@X is an artificial intelligence security organization based in an undisclosed location that provides assessment and certification services to protect enterprise AI systems. The company focuses on building operational confidence in artificial intelligence production environments by evaluating the vulnerabilities of deployed machine learning models. Through its platform at certifies.ai, the entity performs both general system evaluations and targeted attack assessments to deliver actionable security insights. These auditing and compliance services are primarily designed for corporate clients and technology developers requiring rigorous production assurance before deploying automated systems into live commercial environments.
